.amazon_s3: AWS publishes no official OpenAPI/Swagger description for the S3 REST API (only Smithy models in aws/api-models-aws); connector calls signed S3 REST/XML endpoints (https://{bucket}.s3.{region}.amazonaws.com/{key}, ListObjectsV2, GetObject) via ctx.client.
.azure-blob: Azure publishes the Blob Storage data-plane API (blob.json, 2021-12-02) with an empty `paths`: every operation is under the AutoRest `x-ms-paths` extension, keyed with query discriminators such as `?comp=list`, which the recorder and contract mock do not read yet. See https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/296281
.azure_sql: Talks to Azure SQL Database through the mssql driver's TDS protocol, not an HTTP API
.box: Connector does not call the Box REST API through ctx.client; all actions go through the Box remote MCP server (https://mcp.box.com) via withMcpClient. box/box-openapi exists but does not describe the MCP surface.
.brave-search: Brave publishes no downloadable OpenAPI: api-dashboard.search.brave.com has only HTML/markdown API reference and llms.txt, and openapi.json/yaml probes return 404. The only OpenAPI found is a hand-written third-party profile (api-evangelist/brave), not vendor-published.
.databricks: Databricks does not publish its REST API OpenAPI: the databricks-sdk-* repos only pin a .codegen/_openapi_sha and docs.databricks.com/api has no download. The only OpenAPI found is a partial third-party profile (api-evangelist/databricks), not vendor-published, and part of the connector goes through the managed SQL MCP server.
.dropbox: Connector does not call the Dropbox HTTP API through ctx.client; all actions go through the Dropbox remote MCP server (https://mcp.dropbox.com/mcp) via withMcpClient. Dropbox also publishes only Stone specs, not OpenAPI.
.graphql: Generic connector: the endpoint and schema are whatever the user configures, so there is no vendor spec to pin
.monday_com: No OpenAPI: actions go either through the monday.com MCP server (mcp.monday.com/mcp via withMcpClient/callToolJson) or through GraphQL POSTs to https://api.monday.com/v2 (callGraphQL). monday.com publishes a GraphQL schema, not an OpenAPI/Swagger/Discovery document.
.mongodb: Talks to MongoDB through its driver's wire protocol, not an HTTP API
.mysql: Talks to MySQL through its driver's wire protocol, not an HTTP API
.salesforce: No static, vendor-published OpenAPI for the core REST API (/services/data/v66.0/query, /search, /sobjects/{type}/{id}, /sobjects/{type}/describe, /sobjects/ContentVersion/{id}/VersionData). Salesforce's only OpenAPI for sObjects is a beta that each org generates on demand (POST /services/data/vXX.X/async/specifications/oas3), so it depends on the org and needs auth. The API host is also per-org (instanceUrl). APIs.guru has only salesforce.local:einstein, which is not relevant.
.servicenow_search: ServiceNow publishes no public OpenAPI for the Now Platform REST APIs the connector calls (/api/now/table/{table}[/{sys_id}], /api/now/attachment/{sys_id}[/file], /api/now/attachment/file, /api/now/doc/table/schema/{table}, /api/global/em/jsonv2). Each instance has its own host and its own REST API Explorer, and no official static OpenAPI, Swagger or Discovery document exists. APIs.guru has no entry either.
.sharepoint-server: On-premises SharePoint Server REST/OData API (/_api/web, /_api/web/lists/GetByTitle(...)/items, /_api/web/GetFolderByServerRelativeUrl(...), /_api/search/query, plus a generic callRestApi passthrough) on a user-configured site URL. Microsoft publishes no OpenAPI or Swagger for it; only an OData $metadata (CSDL) per farm, which is not an accepted format.
.tavily_mcp: All actions (search, extract, crawl, map, listTools, callTool) and the connector test go through the Tavily MCP server (https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp/) via withMcpClient/callToolJson. No action calls ctx.client HTTP directly.
.workday: Workday REST APIs (/ccx/api/common/v1, /recruiting/v4, /absenceManagement/v5, /holiday/v1 under a per-tenant host and tenant name) have no publicly downloadable OpenAPI. Workday's REST API directory and specs sit behind Workday Community login and are tenant-scoped. APIs.guru has no entry.
.zabbix: JSON-RPC 2.0 API: every call is a POST to a single endpoint ({baseUrl}/api_jsonrpc.php) and the method name is in the request body. Zabbix publishes no OpenAPI/Swagger description, and OpenAPI path templates cannot distinguish its operations.
